name: Armenia
summary: Using drugs without a prescription or possessing small amounts is an administrative offence (fines, higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes. Seeking treatment voluntarily avoids liability for use.
poisonControlNote: No poison information centre is listed for Armenia in WHO's 2023 directory; call 911 or 103 (112 also works from mobiles).
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. People who voluntarily ask a medical facility for help with drug use are released from administrative liability for use.

lsd.note: UN Schedule I. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin is UN Schedule I; how mushrooms are treated was not confirmed. Small amounts: administrative fine.

dmt.note: UN Schedule I (ayahuasca contains DMT). Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

mescaline.note: UN Schedule I; status of cacti not confirmed. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

dox.note: DOM, DOB, DOC are UN Schedule I. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

nbomes.note: UN Schedule I since 2015. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

2c-x.note: 2C-B is UN Schedule II. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T compounds are not UN-controlled; national scheduling not confirmed.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO tryptamines are not UN-controlled; national scheduling not confirmed.

cannabis.note: Use or small-amount possession: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes. No medical cannabis.

ketamine.note: Anaesthetic used in hospitals and veterinary practice; not UN-controlled and national control status not confirmed.

mxe.note: UN Schedule II since 2016. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

dxm.note: Not UN-controlled; national control and prescription status not confirmed.

nitrous.note: Not internationally controlled; no national restriction confirmed.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are UN Schedule II. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

mdma.note: UN Schedule I. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

cocaine.note: Controlled under the 1961 Convention. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes.

alcohol.note: Sale to under-18s is prohibited, though ID checks are rare.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is UN Schedule II (small amounts: administrative fine). GBL/1,4-BD status not confirmed.

opioids.note: Heroin etc. are controlled. Small amounts: administrative fine (higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes. Rx opioids need a prescription.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only painkiller; not UN-controlled and national control status not confirmed.

benzodiazepines.note: UN Schedule IV, prescription-only; using without a prescription is an administrative offence (fine).

maois.note: MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only; harmala/Syrian rue status not confirmed; ayahuasca contains DMT (controlled).
